paper_citation: Ólafsdóttir HF, Carpenter F, Barry C (2016). Coordinated grid and place cell replay during rest. Nature Neuroscience 19, 792-794. https://doi.org/10.1038/nn.4291
apparatus: elevated Z-shaped track (two parallel 190 cm runways joined by a 220 cm diagonal, 10 cm wide), then a cylindrical rest enclosure (18 cm across, 61 cm high) and a 1 m open field

archive.name: Zenodo 5566548
archive.citation: Ólafsdóttir HF, Carpenter F, Barry C (2021). LFP and single-unit data published in Olafsdottir, Carpenter and Barry (2016) Nature Neuroscience 19: 792-794 [Data set]. Zenodo. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.5566548

sampling_rate.source: Ólafsdóttir et al. 2016, Online Methods: 'two light-emitting diodes (LED) mounted on the animals' head-stages (50 Hz)'; each .pos header's sample_rate 50.0 hz

position_span.source: Ólafsdóttir et al. 2016, Online Methods: 'The two parallel sections of the Z (190 cm each) were connected by a diagonal section (220 cm)'. The Z's largest extent along one camera axis runs from 190 cm, its runways along that axis, to 220 cm, rotated; the largest span of the tracked positions must lie between 80% of the first and 120% of the second

speed_limit.source: Iriarte-Díaz 2002, J. Exp. Biol. 205:2897-2908, Table 1: Rattus runs at most 13.78 body lengths/s at a 0.190 m body length, 2.62 m/s (from Garland 1983 and Nowak 1999); times 1.5 because the tracked point is an LED on the head, which swings faster than the body, and no source read states head speed

sessions.verification: Checked by hand on 2026-11-11 against the zip (its MD5 matches Zenodo's), the README and the paper: every tetrode file holds num_spikes x 216 bytes between data_start and data_end with equal timestamps on its four channels; every .cut is 'Exact_cut_for' its own trial with that trial's spike count; the .pos, .eeg and .egf sample counts are duration x 50, 250 and 4800; the track samples, drawn, are a Z with two parallel runways, which the fitted environment follows; the rest starts 159 s after the track ends by the .set times; CA1 ripple power (150-250 Hz) is 10.6 times higher inside the rest's candidate events than outside them, so spikes and LFP share a clock; each unit's spikes are its cluster's marks
